title: ChatGPT Can Now Make GIFs, AI Job Hiring Jumps 32% and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: ChatGPT now turns photos into GIFs, Naukri says AI/ML hiring is up 32%, and India warns banks about AI-powered cyber attacks.
intro: Three AI updates for your Friday: a fun new ChatGPT feature anyone can try, good news for AI job seekers, and a safety warning from India's cybercrime agency.

news.headline: ChatGPT can now turn your photos and ideas into animated GIFs
news.body: OpenAI has rolled out a new image update called Images 2.6 in ChatGPT. The biggest change: you can now ask for a short animated GIF. Type an idea, like a dancing cat, or upload a photo and ask ChatGPT to animate it. You can change how fast the animation plays and edit single frames. OpenAI also says image making is quicker overall. The update is reaching all ChatGPT users on web, desktop and mobile, including the free plan. OpenAI says people now make more than four billion images a week with its tools.
news.why: Small shops and creators can make simple moving greetings, offer posts and WhatsApp stickers for free, without learning any design software.

news.headline: Naukri JobSpeak: AI and machine learning hiring up 32% in October
news.body: Naukri's JobSpeak report for October 2026, released on 3 November, shows white-collar hiring in India grew 14% compared to last year. AI and machine learning roles grew much faster, by 32%. Hyderabad led among cities with 15% growth, followed by Pune and Delhi-NCR. Plain software and testing jobs grew only about 1%. Skills showing up often in AI job posts include GenAI, RAG, vector databases and MLOps. For freshers, entry roles in data operations, QA automation, analyst internships and platform support are said to be the easier way in.
news.why: If you are job hunting, learning to use and build with AI tools is now one of the clearest ways to stand out, even for non-AI roles.

news.headline: India's cybercrime agency warns banks about AI-powered attacks
news.body: The Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the Home Ministry, has warned banks, fintech apps and payment companies that criminals are now using AI agents to break into systems very quickly. CERT-In has also issued related alerts. The warning came days after microfinance lender Spandana Sphoorty reported that nearly Rs 7.8 crore was moved out of one of its bank accounts without permission on 1 November. The advisory asks companies to set transaction limits, check who money is going to, and report attacks within six hours.
news.why: Scammers are getting faster with AI. Never share OTPs or click unknown payment links, and if you lose money, call 1930 or report at cybercrime.gov.in right away.

tip.title: Find the AI skills your dream job wants
tip.body: AI jobs are growing fast, but every job post asks for different skills. Paste a real job post into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude and get a simple learning plan plus resume lines you can honestly use.
tip.prompt: Here is a job post I want to apply for: [paste job post]. My current skills are: [your skills]. 1) List the top 5 skills this job wants, in simple words. 2) Tell me which ones I already have and which I am missing. 3) Give me a 30-day free learning plan for the missing ones, 1 hour a day. 4) Suggest 3 resume bullet points I can use once I finish, without adding anything fake.

title: IndiaAI Launches EKA-1 and Dhir AI Models, WhatsApp AI Chats and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: IndiaAI releases 3 homegrown AI models, WhatsApp tests separate Meta AI chats, Guided Learning comes to Google Classroom.
intro: Three AI updates for today: India's own new AI models, a handy change coming to Meta AI on WhatsApp, and a Gemini study mode that teachers can now add to homework.

news.headline: IndiaAI Mission releases three homegrown AI models: EKA-1, Dhir 2B and Dhir 5B
news.body: On 3 November in New Delhi, MeitY and the IndiaAI Mission unveiled three AI models built in India. EKA-1, from Soket AI Labs, has about 26 billion parameters and covers all 22 scheduled Indian languages plus English. It is meant for maths, coding and reasoning, and for banks that need AI on their own servers, even offline. Dhir 2B and Dhir 5B, from ZenteiQ AiTech, are small models for English and 10 Indian languages. They are built for document search, and can run on a mobile phone offline. Access is through the government's AIKosh platform; Soket says EKA-1's weights will open up within about a month via a waitlist.
news.why: India now has its own AI models that understand Indian languages and can work without internet. Students and developers can try them through AIKosh, and skills in Indian-language AI are becoming a real job area.

news.headline: WhatsApp is testing separate Meta AI chats you can name
news.body: WhatsApp is rolling out a new option to some Android beta testers (version 2.26.44.6). Instead of one long Meta AI conversation, you can start separate Meta AI chats from the menu, give each one a name and even a picture. Each chat keeps its own context, so what you discuss in one does not mix into another. These chats sit in your normal chat list, and a new optional 'AI' filter helps you find them. You can delete them any time. WhatsApp has not said when everyone will get it, so it may take a few weeks to reach regular users.
news.why: If you use Meta AI on WhatsApp, you will soon be able to keep one chat for exam doubts, one for shop replies and one for trip plans, without them getting mixed up.

news.headline: Teachers can now add Gemini's Guided Learning to Google Classroom homework
news.body: Google says teachers can now attach a Guided Learning activity to any assignment in Google Classroom. Guided Learning is a Gemini mode that explains a topic step by step and asks questions, instead of just giving the final answer. Teachers can choose class materials for it to use, see short AI summaries of how the class and each student did, and read student chats. It is rolling out globally from 3 November, in all Gemini-supported languages, for schools on Google Workspace for Education editions, but only where the school admin has switched Gemini on.
news.why: If your school or college uses Google Classroom, you may soon get homework where AI coaches you instead of doing it for you. You can already use Guided Learning yourself in the Gemini app to understand tough chapters.

tip.title: Make AI teach you, not just answer
tip.body: Inspired by today's Guided Learning story: before an exam, ask any AI chatbot to quiz you step by step instead of giving the answers. You learn faster when you try first.
tip.prompt: I am preparing for [exam name, e.g. Class 12 boards / AKTU / SSC]. Teach me [topic] step by step like a patient tutor. Do not give me the full answer at once. Ask me one question at a time, wait for my reply, tell me if I am right, and explain my mistakes in simple English. Start with an easy question and make them harder. After 5 questions, give me a short summary of what I should revise.

title: ChatGPT Lets You Lock Chats With a PIN, Deepfake Curbs and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: ChatGPT can lock private chats, Centre promises deepfake curbs, an Indian voice AI speaks 14 languages, Gemini AI Plus changes.
intro: Four quick AI updates for today: a new privacy feature in ChatGPT, the government's latest word on deepfakes, a Bengaluru startup's multilingual voice AI, and a plan change some Gemini users should know about.

news.headline: ChatGPT now lets you lock private chats behind a PIN
news.body: OpenAI is slowly rolling out a feature called Locked Chats, including for Free and Go users. You can lock any single chat with a four-digit PIN, or with Face ID, fingerprint or your phone unlock on supported devices. Locked chats move into a separate 'Locked chats' area and stop showing in your normal history and search. It works on the web, the phone apps and the new desktop apps. Two warnings: if you forget the PIN and reset it, the locked chats are deleted for good, and locking a chat removes it from any project it was in.
news.why: If you share a phone or laptop with family, you can keep chats about your resume, salary talks or business plans private. Write your PIN somewhere safe, because a reset wipes those chats.

news.headline: Amit Shah promises stronger action against AI deepfakes
news.body: On 2 November, Union Home Minister Amit Shah met actors Chiranjeevi and Ram Charan in Hyderabad, who raised concerns about AI deepfakes being used against artists. Shah said the government will urgently look into the problem, with stronger safeguards and strict penalties, and asked the film industry to send a written representation. Separately, IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has said a consultation paper on AI rules, covering safety and deepfakes, is due in the coming weeks. It is not out yet.
news.why: Fake videos and voice clones are already used in scams. Until new rules arrive, protect yourself: if a 'family member' or 'officer' asks for urgent money on a call or video, hang up and call them back on a number you know. Report fraud on 1930.

news.headline: Bengaluru startup Arrowhead launches Fletch, a voice AI for 14 languages
news.body: Arrowhead AI has launched Fletch, its own text-to-speech model built for customer calls in India and Southeast Asia. It covers 14 languages, including Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali and English, and can switch languages in the middle of a sentence, the way many Indians speak. The company says it starts speaking in under 100 milliseconds and already handles over a million calls a day for clients such as banks and lenders. The accuracy claims come from the company itself.
news.why: The next call from your bank or loan app may be an AI voice in your own language. For job seekers, this shows rising demand for people who can build, test and train AI in Indian languages.

news.headline: Gemini AI Plus users lose Pro models from 13 November
news.body: Google has been emailing people on its lower-priced Gemini AI Plus plan to say that Pro models will no longer be part of that plan from 13 November 2026. After that, Pro models in the Gemini app and in AI Mode will need Google AI Pro or a higher plan. AI Plus will keep the Flash and Flash-Lite models, and old chats that used Pro can carry on with another model. The free plan continues.
news.why: If you pay for AI Plus mainly for Pro answers, check your plan before you renew. For most study notes, emails and everyday questions, the Flash models or the free plan may be enough.

tip.title: Write customer replies in Hinglish
tip.body: Inspired by today's multilingual voice AI story: small shop owners can use any free AI chatbot to write friendly WhatsApp replies in the language their customers actually use. Read it once before sending and fix prices or dates yourself.
tip.prompt: I run a small [type of business] in [city]. A customer sent this message: "[paste customer message]". Write 3 short, polite WhatsApp replies in simple Hinglish (Hindi in English letters). Mention [price/offer/timing] clearly. Keep each reply under 50 words and end with a friendly line asking them to visit or order.

title: Gemini Now Edits PDFs in Chat, IndiaAI Fellowship Deadline and More
summary: Today's AI news in simple words: Gemini can now create and edit PDFs and docs inside chat, IndiaAI Fellowship closes 30 Nov, and Bihar pushes AI in schools.
intro: Three AI updates worth your two minutes today: a handy new Gemini feature for notes and assignments, a paid fellowship Indian AI students should not miss, and a state government telling school staff to start using AI.

news.headline: Gemini can now create and edit PDFs, docs and slides right inside the chat
news.body: Google has added a way to make a file in Gemini and then keep working on it without leaving the conversation. You can, for example, upload photos of handwritten notes and ask for a PDF study guide, see it previewed in the chat, open it full screen, edit it yourself, or highlight one part and ask Gemini to rewrite it. Google says it works wherever the Gemini app is available. PDFs work on phone and web; Google Docs, Sheets, slides and text or code files are web only for now.
news.why: Students can turn class notes into a clean revision PDF in minutes, and small businesses can draft a price list or flyer and fix it line by line instead of starting again each time.

news.headline: IndiaAI Fellowship 2026: applications close 30 November
news.body: The IndiaAI Fellowship under MeitY's IndiaAI Mission supports full-time UG, PG and PhD students in India working on AI. Reported support goes up to ₹1 lakh for undergraduates and ₹2 lakh for postgraduates, with monthly support for eligible PhD scholars. Undergraduates usually need a few AI-related courses to qualify. Reports say there is no application fee, so ignore anyone asking for money to 'guarantee' a seat.
news.why: If you are a B.Tech or MCA student taking AI or ML subjects, this is real money for your project. Read the official notice on fellowship.indiaai.gov.in, get your HoD's signature early, and apply well before the last day.

news.headline: Bihar asks school education staff to use ChatGPT, Claude and other AI tools
news.body: On 2 November, Bihar's Education Department wrote to all District Education Officers asking them to encourage officials and staff in government schools and education offices to use AI apps such as ChatGPT and Claude. The suggested uses are office work: reviewing schemes, organising data and cutting down routine paperwork. It is encouragement, not a strict order, and no training plan was mentioned.
news.why: AI skills are moving from 'nice to have' to expected, even in government offices. Learning to use these tools well now gives you an edge in almost any job.

tip.title: Turn messy notes into a revision sheet
tip.body: Take a clear photo of your handwritten notes, upload it to Gemini, ChatGPT or Claude, and paste this prompt. Always check the answer against your textbook before you trust it.
tip.prompt: These are my class notes on [topic] for my [subject] exam. Turn them into a one-page revision sheet: 5 key points, 3 important definitions, 1 simple diagram described in words, and 5 likely exam questions with short answers. Mark anything in my notes that looks wrong or unclear.
